difficultyReason: Three simple facts establish a direct correlation with one clear hedged inference. The correct answer uses modest language ('at least some') that the data clearly support. Distractors either overreach to 'all' or are out of scope.
stimulus: A longitudinal study tracked 500 regularly employed adults over five years. Those who reported taking at least two weeks of vacation time annually showed lower rates of cardiovascular disease compared to those who took less than one week of vacation time. This relationship held across different age groups and income levels.
questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All adults who take two weeks of vacation annually will avoid cardiovascular disease.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Taking vacation time is the primary cause of good cardiovascular health.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At least some regularly employed adults who take two weeks of vacation annually have lower cardiovascular disease rates than those taking minimal vacation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vacation time must be taken in one consecutive period to reduce cardiovascular risk.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Adults earning higher incomes benefit more from vacation time than lower-income adults.

explanations.correct: The study directly shows that those taking two or more weeks had lower cardiovascular disease rates than those taking less than one week, across multiple demographic groups. The hedged language ('at least some') accurately reflects what the data show without overclaiming causation or universality.
explanations.A: Too strong — the passage never claims all such adults will avoid disease, only that they show lower rates.
explanations.B: Too strong — the data show correlation, not causation, and 'primary cause' overstates the connection.
explanations.D: Out of scope — the stimulus says nothing about whether vacation must be consecutive.
explanations.E: Opposite of what the data support — the stimulus says the relationship held 'across different income levels,' suggesting similar patterns, not that higher earners benefit more.

difficultyReason: Simple observational fact about a subgroup's behavior. Correct answer makes a modest claim about 'some' members of the group. Distractors either generalize to all, invert the finding, or add unsupported causal language.
stimulus: A survey of 300 small business owners in metropolitan areas found that 67 percent use social media as part of their marketing strategy. Among those who use social media, the average business saw an increase in customer inquiries within six months of adoption.
questionStem: The statements above, if true, most support which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All small business owners in metropolitan areas use social media for marketing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Social media adoption is the most effective marketing tool available to small businesses.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some small business owners who use social media saw increases in customer inquiries within six months.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Small business owners who do not use social media will experience fewer customer inquiries.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Using social media guarantees a small business will see increased customer inquiries.

explanations.correct: The stimulus says that among social media users, the average business saw an increase in inquiries. This directly supports that at least some (in fact, many) of those who adopted social media experienced the reported benefit.
explanations.A: Too strong — only 67 percent use it; the passage explicitly contradicts a universal claim.
explanations.B: Too strong — 'most effective' is not supported; the data show only that users saw increases.
explanations.D: Unsupported — the passage says nothing about non-users' outcomes.
explanations.E: Too strong — 'guarantees' overstates what the data show; the passage reports an average increase, not universality.

difficultyReason: Two facts: (1) a linguistic pattern across multiple languages, and (2) a plausible alternative explanation. Correct answer attributes the pattern to a natural constraint without dismissing the alternative. Distractors either assume causation or ignore the stated constraint.
stimulus: Linguists have documented that vowel sounds at the end of words occur more frequently in Romance languages than in Germanic languages. Researchers hypothesize this is partly due to the phonological rules governing syllable structure—Romance languages permit more word-final vowels than Germanic languages. However, historical contact and borrowing patterns between language families may also play a role.
questionStem: Which one of the following inferences is most supported by the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Phonological rules are the sole cause of vowel distribution differences between language families.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some of the difference in word-final vowel frequency between Romance and Germanic languages is at least partly attributable to phonological constraints.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Germanic languages are historically younger than Romance languages.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Historical borrowing has a stronger effect on vowel distribution than phonological rules do.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All vowel sounds in Romance languages derive from contact with Germanic languages.

explanations.correct: The stimulus establishes both (1) an observed difference and (2) a documented phonological explanation for it, while acknowledging other factors may also apply. The hedged language ('at least partly') and acknowledgment of multiple causes fit the facts precisely.
explanations.A: Too strong — the stimulus explicitly mentions contact and borrowing as additional possible factors, so phonology is not the sole cause.
explanations.C: Out of scope — age of languages is not discussed or implied.
explanations.D: Too strong — the stimulus presents both as potentially contributing; it doesn't rank their relative strength.
explanations.E: Too strong and directionally unsupported — the stimulus doesn't claim all Romance vowels derive from Germanic contact.

difficultyReason: Environmental observation: a species shows reduced population in a particular habitat but thrives elsewhere. Correct answer draws the modest inference that the habitat-specific pressure (not universal unsuitability) is the limiting factor. Distractors either universalize or ignore the comparative data.
stimulus: Researchers monitoring populations of a migratory bird species found that nesting numbers in wetland areas of the country have declined by 40 percent over the past decade. However, the same species shows stable or growing populations in forest and grassland habitats during the same period.
questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The bird species is becoming extinct across the country.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Changes in wetland habitat conditions are reducing the suitability of those areas for this bird species.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Forest and grassland habitats are superior to all other habitat types for this species.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The bird species will never return to wetland areas.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wetland conservation efforts have been entirely ineffective.

explanations.correct: The species is thriving elsewhere but declining specifically in wetlands, which most strongly suggests that something about wetland conditions (not the species' overall viability) is the problem. This hedged conclusion respects the comparative data.
explanations.A: Too strong — the species is stable or growing in other habitats, so extinction is not supported.
explanations.C: Too strong and unsupported — the stimulus doesn't compare forest and grassland to 'all other' habitat types.
explanations.D: Too strong — the passage gives no basis for claiming the bird will 'never' return; conditions can change.
explanations.E: Out of scope — the stimulus provides no data on conservation efforts, only on population trends.

difficultyReason: Medical observation: a symptom occurs in multiple disease contexts, suggesting a common mechanism. Correct answer modestly infers a shared feature without claiming universal cause or effect. Distractors either overreach to causation, inverse the finding, or scope-creep.
stimulus: Physicians have observed that patients with several different autoimmune disorders—rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, and celiac disease—all report fatigue as a primary symptom. Laboratory tests show that in each condition, certain immune cells are activated abnormally. Researchers theorize that the abnormal immune activation may be responsible for the fatigue in these conditions.
questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abnormal immune cell activation is the sole cause of fatigue in humans.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some autoimmune disorders with abnormal immune activation produce fatigue as a symptom.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All patients with fatigue have an autoimmune disorder.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Curing abnormal immune activation will eliminate fatigue in all patients.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fatigue can only occur in conditions with abnormal immune cell activation.

explanations.correct: The stimulus documents three autoimmune conditions, each with fatigue and abnormal immune activation. The modest inference that 'some' autoimmune disorders with this activation pattern produce fatigue directly follows from the evidence.
explanations.A: Too strong — the stimulus discusses one possible contributing factor, not the sole cause of all fatigue.
explanations.C: Inverse and too strong — the stimulus doesn't claim all fatigue stems from autoimmune disease.
explanations.D: Too strong — the stimulus posits a possible link, not a guarantee that curing the activation eliminates fatigue.
explanations.E: Too strong and contradicts common knowledge — fatigue has many causes beyond immune activation.

difficultyReason: Economic data: two regions show different adoption rates of a technology and different economic growth rates. Correct answer avoids claiming causation and simply notes the association. Distractors assume causation, invert the relationship, or universalize.
stimulus: Over the past five years, regions that have rapidly adopted digital payment systems show average economic growth rates 2 percent higher than regions with slower adoption. However, both groups of regions include wealthy and less wealthy areas, suggesting adoption levels are not entirely determined by existing wealth.
questionStem: The statements above, if true, most support which one of the following claims?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adopting digital payment systems directly causes economic growth.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All regions with rapid digital payment adoption will experience higher economic growth than those with slower adoption.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some regions with faster digital payment adoption show higher economic growth rates than regions with slower adoption.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Economic growth is impossible in regions that do not rapidly adopt digital payment systems.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Existing regional wealth is the primary factor driving both digital payment adoption and economic growth.

explanations.correct: The stimulus reports that rapid-adoption regions show 2 percent higher growth on average. The modest phrasing 'some regions' accurately reflects this aggregate comparison without claiming universality or causation.
explanations.A: Too strong — the data show correlation, not causation.
explanations.B: Too strong — the passage reports average differences, not that all rapid-adoption regions outperform all slow-adoption regions.
explanations.D: Too strong and unsupported — the passage implies growth occurs in both groups, just at different average rates.
explanations.E: Out of scope — the stimulus explicitly states adoption is not entirely determined by existing wealth, undermining this claim.

difficultyReason: History/policy: a legislative action had documented effects in some areas but documented counterexamples. Correct answer acknowledges the variation without claiming universal outcomes. Distractors either universalize or deny the documented effect.
stimulus: After a city implemented a ban on plastic shopping bags, waste in city landfills decreased by 3 percent over the following year. However, a survey showed that 40 percent of residents began purchasing reusable bags elsewhere, while 30 percent switched to plastic bags from other retailers, and 15 percent shifted to online shopping with plastic packaging.
questionStem: Which one of the following inferences is most supported by the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Plastic bag bans are always effective at reducing overall plastic waste.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The city's plastic bag ban had inconsistent effects, reducing some forms of waste while not eliminating plastic use entirely.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most residents of the city opposed the plastic bag ban.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reusable bags are the only effective solution to plastic waste.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The ban caused a significant increase in overall landfill waste.

explanations.correct: The stimulus documents both a measurable landfill reduction (3 percent) and evidence that residents found multiple workarounds, some of which still involved plastic. This complexity is accurately captured by the claim of 'inconsistent effects.'
explanations.A: Too strong — the passage shows only a 3 percent reduction and multiple workarounds, undermining 'always effective.'
explanations.C: Out of scope — the survey reports behavior, not expressed opposition; many may have complied willingly.
explanations.D: Too strong and unsupported — the passage mentions reusable bags as one consumer choice, not an endorsed solution.
explanations.E: Opposite direction — the passage reports a 3 percent decrease in landfill waste, not an increase.

difficultyReason: Educational data: test performance correlates with a specific study practice. Correct answer hedges the inference to what the data permit ('students who engage in' or 'at least some'). Distractors either claim causation, invert the correlation, or overgeneralize.
stimulus: A study of 200 high school students found that those who engaged in spaced repetition—reviewing material at increasing intervals over several weeks—scored on average 15 percent higher on final exams than students who used massed practice, studying intensively just before exams. The effect was observed across multiple subject areas.
questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Spaced repetition is the only effective study method.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Students who use massed practice are less intelligent than those who use spaced repetition.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At least some students who use spaced repetition perform better on final exams than those using massed practice.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Spaced repetition causes higher test performance in all students.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Massed practice leads to poor long-term retention.

explanations.correct: The study shows that spaced-repetition users scored 15 percent higher on average. This directly supports that at least some students using that method outperformed massed-practice users.
explanations.A: Too strong — the passage discusses one effective method, not exclusivity.
explanations.B: Out of scope — the study measures study method effects, not intelligence.
explanations.D: Too strong — 'all students' overstates an average difference; some may not benefit equally.
explanations.E: Too strong — the passage compares two methods on a final exam but doesn't address long-term retention explicitly.

difficultyReason: Ethical/observational: a professional group exhibits a particular behavior or standard. Correct answer makes a modest inference about the group's typical practice or tendency. Distractors either universalize, invert, or add unsupported motivational claims.
stimulus: A review of codes of conduct at 50 major law firms found that 46 of them explicitly prohibit attorneys from accepting gifts valued above $50 from clients. The remaining four firms have similar prohibitions but set the threshold at $100 or higher. Interviews with partners at these firms indicate the restrictions aim to prevent conflicts of interest.
questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All law firms prohibit attorneys from accepting any gifts from clients whatsoever.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some law firms have adopted gift restrictions to address conflicts of interest.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Law firms that do not restrict gifts will necessarily experience ethical violations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The $50 threshold is the only ethically defensible limit for attorney gifts.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Attorneys at firms without gift restrictions are more corrupt than those at firms with restrictions.

explanations.correct: The stimulus documents that 50 firms have gift restrictions, explicitly states their stated purpose is conflict-of-interest prevention, and reports partner interviews confirming this rationale. This directly supports that some (in fact, most) firms adopted these restrictions for this stated reason.
explanations.A: Too strong — four firms have a $100 threshold, not an absolute prohibition.
explanations.C: Too strong — the stimulus doesn't claim that absence of restrictions 'necessarily' causes violations.
explanations.D: Too strong and unsupported — different firms use different thresholds; the passage doesn't endorse one as uniquely defensible.
explanations.E: Out of scope — the passage discusses policies and stated intent, not attorney corruption or character.

difficultyReason: Technology/arts observation: a creative medium exhibits a documented trend in how practitioners approach it. Correct answer states a modest inference about the trend without claiming universal adoption or superiority. Distractors either universalize, invert, or add historical claims.
stimulus: Analysis of independent music production over the past decade shows that more than 60 percent of new artists use digital audio workstations (DAWs) rather than traditional recording studios. A survey of these artists revealed they cited lower costs, flexibility in scheduling, and ease of editing as their primary reasons for this choice.
questionStem: The statements above, if true, most support which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All successful musicians record using digital audio workstations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Traditional recording studios are no longer used by any professional musicians.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some independent music artists have adopted DAWs at least partly because of practical advantages such as lower cost and scheduling flexibility.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recording quality is superior when using digital audio workstations.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Traditional recording studios will become completely obsolete within the next five years.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that more than 60 percent of new artists use DAWs and that the survey of these artists cited practical reasons. This directly supports that at least some artists adopted DAWs because of cost, scheduling, and editing advantages.
explanations.A: Too strong — the passage discusses new independent artists, not all successful musicians; many established artists may still use studios.
explanations.B: Too strong — the stimulus says 60+ percent use DAWs, which implies studios are still used by others.
explanations.D: Out of scope — the passage reports artists' stated reasons (practical advantages) but does not compare audio quality.
explanations.E: Too strong and speculative — the passage documents a current trend, not a prediction about obsolescence.
